summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, type 1 diabetes, and extensive vascular disease was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and constipation following hemodialysis. She was found to have a large stool impaction and cellulitis at her recent right index finger amputation site, likely exacerbated by poor perfusion. She was treated with IV antibiotics, bowel regimen, and insulin adjustment for hyperglycemia. A CT scan revealed a 1.4 cm metallic foreign body in the cecal fat, of uncertain significance, prompting a recommendation for outpatient colonoscopy. Her symptoms improved, and she was discharged home with plans to complete antibiotics during dialysis and follow up with specialists.
problems: Infection of amputation stump, right upper extremity
Type 1 diabetes mellitus with diabetic nephropathy
